rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: The particle إن is emphatic like an oath, which explains the lām in the response clause.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه: {وإن} تأكيد شبيه # باليمين؛ لذلك دخلت اللام في جوابها

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: The lām prevents إن from making the clause a negation; together they emphasize the matter.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: دخلت اللام مع إن، لأنها لو لم تدخل كان الكلام جحدا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة
rows.claim: They say the transfer of the direction of prayer to the Kaaba was difficult and weighty.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس (¬3) ومجاهد (¬4) وقتادة (¬5): وقد كانت التولية إلى الكعبة لكبيرة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: He explains the difficulty as the burden of praying toward the Kaaba, except for those God guided.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد (¬6): وقد كانت الصلاة إلى الكعبة لكبيرة ثقيلة، إلا على الذين هدى الله

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: He takes the difficult qibla to mean the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: وإن كانت القبلة لكبيرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative interpretation takes the qibla as Jerusalem: following it was hard except for those God guided.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه يعني: بيت المقدس (¬8)، أي: وإن كان اتباعها لكبيرا إلا على الذين هدى الله

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: After the qibla changed, Jews argued Muslims who had died praying toward Jerusalem had died astray; their relatives asked the Prophet, and the verse reassured them that their faith in the former qibla would not be lost.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: قالت اليهود للمسلمين لما حولت القبلة إلى الكعبة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The plural address to living Muslims includes their deceased fellow believers, so their faith is called “your faith”; he compares this to addressing survivors about people killed from among them.
rows.anchor: وإنما أضيف إلى الأحياء؛ لأن الذين ماتوا على القبلة الأولى كانوا منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise may also be read universally as covering the faith of both living and dead believers.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يحمل على العموم، بأن أراد: إيمان الأحياء والأموات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raʾfa is narrower and gentler than mercy.
rows.anchor: الرأفة: أخص من # الرحمة وأرق

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He notes the two vocalized forms رأفة and رأفة as a lexical alternation, like كأبة and كآبة.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: الرأفة والرآفة، مثل: الكأبة والكآبة

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: He attests several Arabic verb forms for showing raʾfa toward someone.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: رأفت بالرجل، أرأف به رأفة، ورآفة، ورؤفت أرؤف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word رؤوف has two readings: رؤوف on the faʿūl pattern and رؤف on the raʿaf pattern.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: رؤوف على وزن فعول. والثانية: رؤف على وزن رعف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faʿūl reading is preferable because it is more common in Arabic and divine attributes use this pattern, unlike the relatively uncommon faʿil pattern.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ على فعول؛ فلأنه أكثر في كلامهم من فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses رؤوفا, illustrating the faʿūl reading and its suitability among divine attributes.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: نطيع إلهنا ونطيع ربا ... هو الرحمن كان بنا رؤوفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The raʿaf-pattern reading is said to predominate in Hijaz speech; a line by al-Walīd ibn ʿUqba attests it.
rows.anchor: فقد قيل: إنه غالب لغة أهل الحجاز، ومنه قول الوليد بن عقبة بن أبي معيط

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarir’s verse shows that the raʿaf-pattern form became common beyond the Hijaz as well.
rows.anchor: وكثر ذلك حتى قاله غيرهم، قال جرير: ترى للمسلمين عليك حقا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He says patience in obligatory duties and the five prayers at their appointed times help seekers of the afterlife and cleanse sins.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: استعينوا على طلب الآخرة بالصبر على الفرائض، وبالصلوات الخمس في مواقيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience means restraint: holding oneself back from desires and forbidden things and keeping oneself to acts of obedience.
rows.anchor: فالاستعانة بالصبر هو أن يستعين على دينه بحبس النفس عن (¬5) الشهوات والمحارم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Prayer helps because its recitation makes worshippers recognize the merit of the path they follow.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: أي: أنكم إذا صليتم تلوتم في صلاتكم ما تعرفون به فضل ما أنتم عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Through ʿAṭāʾ, Ibn ʿAbbās explains God’s being with the patient as support: He will aid and not abandon them.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء، عن ابن عباس: يقول: إني معكم أنصركم ولا أخذلكم

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: God’s being with them means He will make their religion prevail over other religions; God’s party is victorious.
rows.anchor: تأويله: أنه يظهر دينهم على سائر الأديان؛ لأن من كان الله معه فهو الغالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ordinary language, unity is singleness or separation; a true unit is something that cannot be divided.
rows.anchor: معنى الوحدة في اللغة: هي الانفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “One” can be used as a judgment about indivisible reality or as a descriptive, relative attribute; a human is one as a human but divisible as a body.
rows.anchor: والثاني: على الوصف والمجاز. فالحكم كقولك: ذات واحدة

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: One meaning of God’s oneness is that He has no peer and nothing resembles Him; Arabs call an unmatched person the one of his people.
rows.anchor: له معنيان: أحدهما: أنه واحد لا نظير له، وليس كمثله شيء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God alone is deity and lord, without a partner in divinity or lordship, contradicting the polytheists.
rows.anchor: المعنى في الواحد: أنه إله واحد، ورب واحد، ليس له في إلاهيته وربوبيته شريك

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: “One” is either a number-noun or a descriptor; applied to God it can be a description like knowing and powerful, or a noun like thing, and the verse supports the descriptive use.
rows.anchor: يقوي الأول قوله: {وإلهكم إله واحد}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited line attests the dual form واحدين, used of a unified group.
rows.anchor: فقد (¬5) رجعوا كحي واحدينا (¬6)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural of واحد can follow فعلان as وحدان, and the initial wāw may shift to hamza as أحدان.
rows.anchor: ويكسرونه على فعلان، كقولهم: وحدان، ويقلبون الواو همزة، كقولهم: أحدان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد
rows.claim: They explain completing Hajj and Umrah as performing their rites, limits, sunnas, and every required act.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1) ومجاهد (¬2): أتموهما بمناسكهما وحدودهما

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود، علي، سعيد بن جبير، طاوس
rows.claim: They say completion means beginning both rites from one’s own home, setting out in consecration from there.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود (¬4) وعلي (¬5) رضي الله عنهما: إتمامهما: أن تحرم

rows.speaker: علي، ابن عباس، الشافعي
rows.claim: The first legal view makes Umrah obligatory; it is attributed to ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās and is al-Shāfiʿī’s later position.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أنها (¬1) واجبة، وهو مذهب علي (¬2) وابن عباس (¬3)، وقول الشافعي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He swears that scripture pairs Umrah with Hajj, supporting its obligation.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: والله إن العمرة لقرينة الحج في كتاب الله

rows.speaker: مسروق
rows.claim: He compares Umrah’s place beside Hajj to zakat’s place beside prayer, then cites this verse.
rows.anchor: وقال مسروق: نزلت العمرة من الحج منزلة الزكاة من الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who require Umrah read “complete” as “begin and perform”: the verb can mean to undertake and carry through an act, as in the trials of Abraham and the fast.
rows.anchor: فمن أوجب العمرة تأول الإتمام على معنى الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hajj has four obligatory pillars: consecration, standing at ʿArafāt, the circumambulation of ifāḍa, and saʿy.
rows.anchor: وفرائض الحج أربعة: الإحرام، والوقوف، وطواف الإفاضة، والسعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umrah consists of consecration, circumambulation, saʿy, and shaving or shortening; the minimum is three hairs.
rows.anchor: وأعمال العمرة: الإحرام، والطواف، والسعي، والحلق والتقصير (¬3)، وأقله: ثلاث شعرات

rows.speaker: أهل العراق
rows.claim: The second view treats Umrah as sunnah rather than obligatory and reads completion as finishing it once one has started, as with voluntary Hajj.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني: أن العمرة سنة وليست بفريضة، وهو مذهب أهل العراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first view is stronger because it combines both senses: initiate Umrah, then complete it; one can tell someone to complete a task before they start it.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول أولى لأن فيه جمعا بين وجهي الإتمام

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: He distinguishes the verbs: being turned away from an intended destination is أحصر, while being confined is حصر.
rows.anchor: عن يونس، قال: إذا رد الرجل عن وجه يريده فقد أحصر، وإذا حبس فقد حصر

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: He uses أحصر for illness preventing travel or a desired need, and حصر for an enemy constricting someone.
rows.anchor: عن ابن السكيت (¬5): أحصره المرض: إذا منعه من السفر أو من حاجة يريدها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Lexical authorities use أحصر for prevention by fear or illness, and حصر for someone imprisoned.
rows.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق الزجاج، قال: الرواية عن أهل اللغة للذي يمنعه الخوف أو المرض

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: He defines أحصر as any illness, fracture, or enemy obstacle preventing Hajj, while a person jailed in prison or a house is حصر.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة في قوله: {فإن أحصرتم}: هو أن يعرض للرجل ما يحول بينه وبين الحج

rows.speaker: الفراء، أبو عبيد عن أبي عبيدة
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ’s lexical view, also cited by Abū ʿUbayd from Abū ʿUbayda, follows the distinction between prevention and confinement.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو قول الفراء في المصادر، ونحو (¬5) ذلك ذكر أبو عبيد عن أبي عبيدة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Some authorities treat the two forms as synonymous; al-Zajjāj gives parallel questions using حصرك and أحصرك.
rows.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أنهما بمعنى واحد، قال الزجاج، في باب الوفاق

rows.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
rows.claim: He says both derive from confinement, with حصر the stronger form for imprisonment.
rows.anchor: وقال أحمد بن يحيى: أصل الحصر والإحصار: الحبس، وحصر في # الحبس أقوى من أحصر

rows.speaker: الأزهري عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Azharī reports as sound Ibn ʿAbbās’s statement that only enemy confinement is ḥaṣr; the unprefixed form can convey the verse’s sense.
rows.anchor: وقال الأزهري: الرواية عن ابن عباس صحيحة أنه قال: لا حصر (¬2) إلا حصر العدو

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He distinguishes fear or illness as أحصر and forcible imprisonment as حصر, while allowing either form when the intended cause is construed differently.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: يقال للذي يمنعه خوف أو مرض: أحصر، ولمن حبس قهرا: حصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root meaning is confinement; even a secretive person is called حصرة because he restrains himself from disclosure, as in Jarīr’s poem.
rows.anchor: وأصل الباب: الحبس، ومنه يقال للذي لا يبوح بسره: حصرة لأنه حبس نفسه عن البوح

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarīr’s line uses حصرا for someone who guards a secret, illustrating the root sense of restraint.
rows.anchor: قال # جرير: ولقد تكنفني الوشاة فصادفوا ... حصرا بسرك يا أميم ضنينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حصر also means constipation; الحصير can mean a king confined behind a veil or a reed mat whose pieces are bound together, and a person lying on his side is called حصير by analogy.
rows.anchor: والحصر: احتباس الغائط، والحصير: الملك؛ لأنه كالمحبوس في الحجاب

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labīd’s line attests الحصير in the sense of king.
rows.anchor: وهو في شعر لبيد: جن لدى باب الحصير قيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Iraqi school counts every impediment to reaching the sanctuary, including illness, injury, fracture, enemy fear, or any other barrier, as ihṣār; the pilgrim remains consecrated, sends a sacrifice or its price, and exits after slaughter.
rows.anchor: فمذهب أهل العراق: أن كل مانع منع المحرم عن الوصول إلى البيت من: مرض أو جرح أو كسر أو خوف عدو

rows.speaker: أهل العراق
rows.claim: They argue that the wording of ihṣār is general and therefore covers every impediment.
rows.anchor: واحتجوا بأن الإحصار من طريق اللفظ عام # في كل مانع

rows.speaker: أهل الحجاز، الشافعي
rows.claim: The Hijazi school, including al-Shāfiʿī, limits the ruling to enemy detention; it cites the Hudaybiyya occasion and the following phrase “when you are safe,” which points to fear of enemies rather than recovery from illness.
rows.anchor: أن الحكم المتعلق بالإحصار إنما يتعلق بحبس العدو عن الوصول إلى البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported reason for revelation is the enemy’s detention of the Prophet and his Companions at al-Ḥudaybiyya, supporting the enemy-specific reading.
rows.anchor: والدليل على (¬4) هذا سبب النزول، وهو إحصار العدو للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وأصحابه بالحديبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of illness in the next clause shows that ihṣār in the opening clause is not illness; Ibn ʿAbbās also restricts ḥaṣr to enemy detention.
rows.anchor: فعلم أن الإحصار في الآية ليس بالمرض، وأيضا ذكرنا عن ابن عباس أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the term is generally worded, contextual evidence makes it specific here to enemy detention that bars access to the House.
rows.anchor: هو عام من حيث اللفظ، خاص ههنا في حبس العدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once consecrated for Hajj or Umrah, a person must complete the rite even if sexual intercourse invalidates it; only enemy ihṣār permits release, as happened to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: حتى لو أفسد الإحرام بالجماع وجب عليه المضي في فاسد الإحرام

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: For an obligatory Hajj or Umrah blocked by an enemy or ruler, al-Shāfiʿī requires sacrifice and release at the place of detention, followed by a make-up rite when the blockade ends; voluntary rites do not require make-up, though it is recommended.
rows.anchor: فقال الشافعي: إذا أحصر بعدو كافر أو مسلم، أو سلطان يحبسه في سجن

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī gives two views for a person unable to obtain a sacrifice: he either cannot leave consecration without one or may leave and offer it when able.
rows.anchor: وإذا لم يجد هديا يشتريه، أو كان فقيرا، ففيه قولان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person prevented by illness remains in consecration, though necessary treatment and expiation are allowed.
rows.anchor: وأما المحصر بالمرض، فإنه يصير على إحرامه ولا يتحلل، وله أن يتداوى بما لابد منه ويفتدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse omits the phrase “from completing Hajj and Umrah”; the preceding context makes the ellipsis clear.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إضمار، تقديره: فإن أحصرتم دون تمام الحج والعمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun ما is nominative, yielding “what is available is obligatory for you.”
rows.anchor: محل "ما" رفع. المعنى: فواجب عليكم ما استيسر

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He allows an accusative reading in the sense “offer what is available,” though the Qurʾān more often uses the nominative in comparable constructions.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: ولو نصبت على معنى: اهدوا ما استيسر، كان صوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: استيسر means تيسر, just as استعظم means تعظم and استكبر means تكبر.
rows.anchor: واستيسر بمعنى: تيسر، ومثله استعظم، أي: تعظم، واستكبر، أي: تكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هدي is a plural of هدية, like شرية/شري and جدية/جدي.
rows.anchor: والهدي: جمع هدية، مثل: شرية وشري، وجدية وجدي

rows.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
rows.claim: The Hijazis lighten الهدي while Tamīm doubles it, as in هدية and هدي.
rows.anchor: قال أحمد بن يحيى: أهل الحجاز يخففون الهدي، وتميم تثقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem swearing by Mecca and the sanctuary mentions sacrificial animals adorned with collars, attesting the term الهدي.
rows.anchor: حلفت برب مكة والمصلى ... وأعناق الهدي مقلدات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hady is what is offered to God’s House as devotion, like a gift offered to another as a means of drawing near.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الهدي: ما يهدى إلى بيت الله عز وجل تقربا إليه

rows.speaker: علي، ابن عباس، الحسن، قتادة
rows.claim: They rank the available offerings as camel, then cow, then sheep, and require whatever of these kinds a person can afford.
rows.anchor: قال علي (¬6) وابن # عباس (¬1) والحسن (¬2) وقتادة (¬3) في هذه الآية: أعلاه بدنة، وأوسطه بقرة، وأخسه شاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One must not leave consecration until the sacrifice is slaughtered; “reaches its place” means the place or time at which slaughter becomes lawful.
rows.anchor: أي: لا تتحللوا من إحرامكم حتى ينحر الهدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term maḥill can mean when or where something becomes lawful; the text gives the relevant lexical forms and an example of usage.
rows.anchor: ومعنى {حتى يبلغ الهدي محله} أي: حيث يحل ذبحه ونحره

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In the report about meat given to Burayra, the Prophet says it has reached its place: it became lawful for him as a gift after having been charity to her.
rows.anchor: كقوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في اللحم الذي تصدق على بريرة: "قربوه فقد بلغ محله"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and his Companions slaughtered their sacrifices at al-Ḥudaybiyya, outside the sacred precinct, when barred from the House.
rows.anchor: وهكذا فعل النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وأصحابه، حين صدوا عن البيت، نحروا هديهم بالحديبية ليست من الحرم

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī requires other obligatory offerings from a pilgrim’s wealth to be slaughtered for the sanctuary’s poor, except a sacrifice for enemy detention and an animal that collapses en route.
rows.anchor: وكل ما وجب على المحرم في ماله من بدنة وجزاء وهدي فلا يجزي إلا في الحرم

rows.speaker: أهل العراق
rows.claim: The Iraqi school places the detained pilgrim’s sacrifice in the sanctuary: on the sacrifice day for Hajj, or when the animal reaches the sanctuary for Umrah.
rows.anchor: وعلى مذهب أهل العراق محل # هدي المحصر الحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The underlying disagreement is whether maḥill here means the time when sacrifice is lawful, as the Hijazis say, or its location, as others say.
rows.anchor: حقيقة الخلاف تعود إلى أن عند أهل الحجاز المحل في هذه الآية اسما للأوان

rows.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
rows.claim: At al-Ḥudaybiyya, lice and nits from Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra’s long hair fell onto his face as he cooked; the Prophet asked if his head vermin troubled him and told him to shave, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: نزلت في كعب ابن عجرة (¬4) قال: مر بي رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - زمن الحديبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pilgrim shaves or treats the condition, he owes a fidya to repair the defect caused in consecration.
rows.anchor: فحلق أو فداوى فعليه فدية يفدي بها إحرامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illness or head vermin permits shaving and treatment with a choice of expiations: three fasting days anywhere, feeding six poor people two mudd each (twelve mudd total), or sacrifice; the normal food amount in other expiations is one mudd per person.
rows.anchor: وهذه الفدية على التخيير أيها شاء فعل، كما دل عليه ظاهر الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion of the word ṣadaqa is deferred to the explanation of 2:271.
rows.anchor: وأصل معنى الصدقة نذكرها في قوله: {إن تبدوا الصدقات}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nusuk is a sacrifice slaughtered for God; its root means worship, and a worshipper is a nāsik. Ibn al-Aʿrābī also explains nasīka as a silver ingot, likening worship to purification from sin and the sacrifice to a noble act of devotion.
rows.anchor: وأصل النسك: العبادة. والناسك: العابد. قال ابن الأعرابي: النسك سبائك الفضة

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars rank the sacrifice as camel, cow, then sheep, and say the pilgrim may choose among these kinds.
rows.anchor: قال العلماء أعلاها: بدنة، وأوسطها: بقرة، وأدناها: شاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The food and sacrifice expiations may be offered anywhere because the verse leaves their location unrestricted.
rows.anchor: والصحيح: أنه يأتي بالإطعام والنسك أي موضع شاء، لأن الله تعالى أطلق في الآية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He explains safety as either safety from an enemy or a Hajj with no enemy present; both circumstances fall under the rule for tamattuʿ.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أي من العدو، أو كان حج ليس فيه عدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matāʿ is anything one benefits from; the word is associated with something tall and with prolonged companionship.
rows.anchor: والمتاع: كل شيء يتمتع به، وينتفع به. وأصله: من قولهم: جبل ماتع، أي: طويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamattuʿ is entering Mecca in consecration, performing Umrah during the Hajj months, then living outside consecration until performing Hajj in that same year; the interval permits enjoyment of ihram’s former prohibitions.
rows.anchor: والتمتع بالعمرة إلى الحج هو: أن يقدم مكة محرما، فيعتمر في أشهر الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “by the Umrah” is causal: the pilgrim does not enjoy the Umrah itself but enjoys release from ihram restrictions because of it.
rows.anchor: ومعنى قوله: {بالعمرة} هو أي: بسبب العمرة، لأنه لا يتمتع بالعمرة

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Their conditions for an obligatory tamattuʿ sacrifice are: Umrah and release in the Hajj months, beginning Hajj from Mecca that same year without returning to the miqat, and not being a resident of the sanctuary; missing any condition removes the sacrifice obligation and the status of tamattuʿ.
rows.anchor: قال أصحابنا: المتمتع الذي يجب عليه الدم: هو الذي يحم في أشهر الحج

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: When all conditions hold, the pilgrim must sacrifice, either before or on the sacrifice day; a wealthy person cannot substitute another act, while a poor person fasts ten days.
rows.anchor: وإذا وجدت هذه الشرائط كان متمتعا، وعليه إراقة دم إن شاء قبل يوم النحر

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: They specify the three Hajj-month fasts as the day before the Day of Tarwiya, the Day of Tarwiya, and the Day of ʿArafa.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: يصوم يوما قبل التروية، ويوم التروية، ويوم عرفة

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The three fasts must precede the sacrifice day and may be consecutive or separate; it is better to finish before ʿArafa and be fasting-free on that day, since the Prophet did not fast then and that is stronger for supplication.
rows.anchor: قال أصحابنا: يصوم ثلاثة أيام قبل يوم النحر في أشهر الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven fasts may be kept anywhere and at any time after completing Hajj; it is preferable to avoid the Days of Tashriq, and missed Hajj-month fasts are made up later.
rows.anchor: أما السبعة فله أن يصومها بعد الفراغ من الحج، أين شاء ومتى شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb كمل is reported with more than one present-tense vocalization.
rows.anchor: يقال: كمل الشيء يكمل، وكمل يكمل، فهو كامل وكميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Ten complete” reinforces the total even though three plus seven plainly equals ten; a line by al-Farazdaq illustrates such emphasis.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال: {تلك عشرة كاملة} مع العلم بأن الثلاثة والسبعة عشرة، # للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An explanation says Arabs were an unlettered people unfamiliar with arithmetic, citing Jābir’s count of the people at al-Ḥudaybiyya and an unnamed Companion who thought one thousand was the highest number.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن العرب أمة أمية، لا تعرف الحساب

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Because Arabic waw may mean “or,” as in 4:3, al-Zajjāj says the verse clarifies that all ten fasts are required, not either three or seven.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: العرب قد تذكر الواو والمراد منها أو

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation calls the ten a complete substitute for the sacrifice even though the days are divided between Hajj and home.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد: كاملة في البدل عن الدم، وإن كانت مفرقة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation treats the statement as an imperative in meaning: complete all ten without reducing them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لفظه خبر ومعناه أمر، أي: فأكملوها ولا تنقصوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage also links the thirty nights plus ten for Moses to the total forty.
rows.anchor: وواعدنا موسى ثلاثين ليلة وأتممناها بعشر فتم ميقات ربه أربعين ليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sacrifice or fasting obligation applies to outsiders rather than residents of Mecca.
rows.anchor: أي: ذلك الفرض والذي أمرنا به لمن كان من الغرباء من غير أهل مكة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The lām in لمن means “upon,” so the sacrifice or fast is incumbent upon the non-Meccan; the wording is compared with the Prophetic instruction about stipulating loyalty.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: واللام في قوله: {لمن} معناها: على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Their family” refers to the person’s residence, not the family itself, since people generally live where their families live.
rows.anchor: والله تعالى ذكر الأهل والمراد بالحضور المحرم لا الأهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Residents are those whose homes are within a distance that does not permit shortening prayer; they are called present because they live near Mecca.
rows.anchor: والحاضرون: من كانت داره على مسافة لا يقصر إليها الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of ḥarām means prevention: the sanctuary is protected from forbidden acts and unauthorized entry; maḥrūm means one prevented from earnings.
rows.anchor: أصل الحرام: المنع، والمحروم: الممنوع من المكاسب

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr’s phrase لا غائب مالي ولا حرم uses ḥaram to mean something withheld or prohibited.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول زهير: لا غائب مالي ولا حرم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ notes the variant forms حرام and حرم, like زمان and زمن.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: ويقال حرام وحرم، مثل: زمان وزمن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Fearing God here means fulfilling what He has made obligatory; the severe punishment is for those who neglect His limits.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد فيما افترضه عليكم {واعلموا أن الله شديد العقاب} لمن تهاون بحدوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laghw literally means speech with no benefit that is not counted; the text distinguishes the verbal forms and their verbal nouns.
rows.anchor: اللغو: معناه في اللغة: الكلام الذي لا فائدة فيه ولا يعتد به

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ distinguishes اللغا as the verbal noun of لغيت from اللغو as the verbal noun of لغوت.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء. اللغا مصدر للغيت، واللغو مصدر للغوت

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj’s verse uses اللغا for idle speech, as in pilgrims refraining from it and sexual talk.
rows.anchor: قال العجاج: ورب أسراب حجيج كظم ... عن اللغا ورفث التكلم

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhū al-Rumma’s verse uses لغوا for something cast aside as irrelevant.
rows.anchor: وقال ذو الرمة: ويطرح بينها المرئي لغوا

rows.speaker: ابن المظفر
rows.claim: He lists related forms including اللغو، اللاغية، اللواغي، اللغا، and اللغوي.
rows.anchor: قال ابن المظفر: يقول: اللغو واللاغية واللواغي واللغا واللغوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says that telling a companion “be quiet” while the Friday preacher speaks makes one commit laghw.
rows.anchor: ومنه الحديث: "من قال يوم الجمعة لصاحبه صه (¬6) والإمام يخطب فقد لغا (¬7) "

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: He defines laghw as words thrown away because they are unnecessary; al-Kumayt’s verse illustrates setting something aside without intention.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: اللغو عند العرب: ما يطرح من الكلام (¬1) استغناء عنه

rows.speaker: الكميت
rows.claim: Al-Kumayt’s line says the events were not forgotten as idle talk nor deliberately put forward.
rows.anchor: قال الكميت: وبعد ذلك (¬2) أيام (¬3) سنذكرها ... لم تنس لغوا ولم تقدم على عمد (¬4)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A bird’s call is called laghw because its intended meaning cannot be understood; an anonymous line supplies the usage.
rows.anchor: ويقال: لغا الطائر يلغو لغوا: إذا صوت، وسمي ذلك منه لغوا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj includes any speech without good, whether sinful or simply unnecessary, under laghw.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: وكل ما لا خير فيه مما يؤثم فيه، أو يكون غير محتاج إليه في الكلام فهو لغو

rows.speaker: مجاهد، عكرمة، الشعبي
rows.claim: They define oath-laghw as a phrase that slips out without a deliberate oath or intention, such as conversational “no, by God” or “yes, by God”; it carries neither expiation nor sin.
rows.anchor: فقال مجاهد (¬1) وعكرمة (¬2) والشعبي (¬3): لغو اليمين، في هذه الآية، ما يسبق به اللسان من غير عقد ولا قصد

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: She includes oaths made jokingly, in argument, or during quarrels, when the heart did not intend to bind itself; Ḥammād transmits a similar view from Ibrāhīm.
rows.anchor: وهو قول عائشة رضى الله عنها، قالت: أيمان اللغو ما كان في الهزل والمراء والخصومة

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: A similar explanation is transmitted from Ibrāhīm through Ḥammād: such utterances are not intended by the heart.
rows.anchor: ومثله روى حماد (¬5) عن إبراهيم (¬6)، وهو كما روي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In a report about archers, when one man swore he had hit and another said he missed, a Companion thought an oath had been broken; the Prophet ruled that archers’ oaths are laghw, with no expiation or penalty.
rows.anchor: فقال الذي مع النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام: حنث الرجل يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: The author says al-Farazdaq intended this sense of unbound oath when he used a line, but the line is not included in this segment.
rows.anchor: وكأن الفرزدق أراد هذا المعنى بقوله
